author: gaxanh
content:
<@508125616940515329> 
> Are there use cases for different code being deposited to the same account? How would this pattern look like? (within 2 different transactions)

Initially, I wanted temporary accounts to be able to handle callbacks. However, this would effectively give temporary accounts the same functionality as persistent accounts, except that they would only exist for the duration of a transaction. This functionality is already possible with CREATEx/SELFDESTRUCT, but the cost is currently too high.

author: gaxanh
content:
I think if the idea of temporary accounts had come up earlier, EIP-1014 might have introduced TCREATE instead of CREATE2.

With TCREATE, we can emulate all of the deployment patterns currently available on the network using just the TCREATE/CREATE pair. Therefore, prohibiting CREATE2 would be reasonable if the goal is to simplify deployment semantics.

A more radical idea would be to change CREATE2 so that the created account is automatically deleted at the end of the transaction. However, this would break existing CREATE2 factories.

In that model:

CREATE3: TCREATE → CREATE

CREATE2: Similar to CREATE3, but fix the initcode.
